text:
Priya (PM): Hey team — putting up the mock for the 'empty eval run' state in Prompt Sets. TL;DR: new empty-run helptray that nudges users to create a prompt set or import tests. Screenshot: https://img.prod/mock/empty-run-1.png :eyes: Alex (Design): Nice! main question: should primary CTA be 'Create test' or 'Create prompt set'? Priya (PM): Leaning 'Create prompt set' because that's what shows up in onboarding copy. But worried it's ambiguous for power users who expect 'Create test run'. Alex (Design): What if we do two actions? Primary 'Create prompt set' + secondary 'Run quick test' (less emphasis). Jordan (Eng): Two CTAs is fine technically. Need to know expected conversion — we can add a flag in the client to hide the secondary if metrics show noise. Sam (Accessibility): A few a11y nits — the helptray appears via animation; we need to ensure focus lands inside and there is an accessible dismiss. Also aria-live for the helper text when it loads. Marco (Frontend): Noted. I'll add focus-trap and make the close button first tabbable element. For aria-live: set role="status" and aria-live="polite" on the main body. Alex (Design): Also visual contrast — the CTA on the mock is light blue on a pale bg; low contrast for low-vision users. Increase weight or outline. Priya (PM): Good catch. Alex, can you propose two color options? high-contrast and subtle? Alex (Design): Yup. Option A: stronger blue (#0B63D6) on white. Option B: white text on dark navy pill. I'll drop comps in Figma. Tay (Product): One more product flow question — when someone clicks 'Run quick test' from empty state, do we create a default prompt set for them or open a modal to configure? Jordan (Eng): Backend prefers creating a lightweight ephemeral prompt set to keep UX fast. We can surface a banner that it's auto-created and allow edit later. Priya (PM): Ok. Make the ephemeral set editable from the run summary. Sam (Accessibility): Microcopy: instead of 'Run quick test' use 'Quick run' — shorter but ambiguous. 'Run example test' might be clearer for screenreader users. Also ensure link text doesn't say 'click here'. Alex (Design): Agree — use 'Run example test' for SR clarity, and visually show 'Quick run' in the button with aria-label="Run example test". Marco (Frontend): Example snippet I'll implement: ```
No runs yet — create a prompt set to get started.
``` Priya (PM): Love the snippet. One more thing: the empty-run page currently infinite-scrolls the run list; for true empty state we should show the helptray full width and hide the list until at least one run exists. Jordan (Eng): Hiding the list is cheap. But infinite-scroll causes layout shifts when new runs appear; we should reserve space or use skeleton placeholders to avoid jumpiness. Marco (Frontend): I'll add a skeleton that preserves height. Also respect prefers-reduced-motion for the helptray entrance. CSS example: ``` @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .helptray { transition: none; } } ``` Sam (Accessibility): For keyboard users, ensure the primary CTA is reachable via tab and that after action the focus goes to the run summary. Use focus management: focusElement.focus() after navigation. Alex (Design): UX copy suggestion for helptray body: 'No evaluation runs yet. Create a prompt set to start testing variations of your prompts, or run a sample test to see results instantly.' Shorten if needed. Priya (PM): Drafting final copy: 'No runs yet — create a prompt set to start testing, or run a sample test to see results.' We'll iterate in the PR. Tay (Product): Analytics: add event names: `empty_run_create_prompt_set` and `empty_run_quick_test` with an optional `created_ephemeral=true` flag. Jordan (Eng): Will add client events. For rollout, GA behind feature flag `empty_run_helptray_v2` — then we can A/B test wording. Marco (Frontend): I'll send a PR with: helptray, skeleton placeholder, focus trap, aria-live, and prefers-reduced-motion handling. Priya (PM): Timeline: aiming to ship the front-end bits next week. Can everyone review the PR when Marco posts? design-bot: New design files uploaded by Alex. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/empty-run-helptray Alex (Design): Uploaded two color options and a small keyboard journey gif. :sparkles: Sam (Accessibility): I'll do a quick a11y pass on the PR after it's up. Add me to reviewers. Jordan (Eng): I'll test skeleton behavior with large datasets to ensure no perf regressions. Priya (PM): Thanks all — great feedback. I'll follow up with copy + analytics spec in the thread. :thumbsup:
